target.title: fix(cli): silent drop of malformed post-core install-records JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw update` post-core resume would silently lose parent plugin install-records recovery context when the handoff file contained malformed JSON (or was unreadable for a non-missing reason). The reader returned `undefined`, so an empty post-doctor index caused the update to continue without that snapshot and without an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Missing handoff files remain optional (`ENOENT` / omitted path → `undefined`). Corrupt JSON and other read failures now fail closed with a path-labelled error, matching the CLI malformed-JSON pattern used by secrets plan apply. Valid maps still normalize through the existing install-record helper.

## User Impact

A corrupt post-core install-records handoff no longer disappears quietly during update resume; operators get a clear malformed/unreadable path error instead of proceeding without parent recovery context.

## Evidence

| Layer | Proof | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | omitted / missing → `undefined`; valid map loads; malformed throws path-labelled error | pass |
| L2 | exported handoff reader owns the post-core install-records boundary; `updateCommand` post-core resume calls it before plugin convergence | pass |
| L3 | real child-process post-core resume (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE=1` + malformed handoff) → path-labelled error, non-zero exit | pass |

### Before (current main catch-all)

Malformed handoff is swallowed → `undefined` (silent loss of parent recovery context).

```text
[before main catch-all] path=/tmp/…/plugin-install-records.json result=undefined
```

### After (this PR) — real post-core resume child process

Same env contract as `continuePostCoreUpdateInFreshProcess` (`OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE=1`, channel `dev`, install-records path). Child process invokes `updateCommand({ restart: false, yes: true })` against a real malformed file (`{not-json`).

```text

cause=Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
[post-core install-records CLI proof] path=/tmp/…/plugin-install-records.json exit=1 outcome=malformed-json-rejected
```

target.title: fix(e2e): bound docker package-install and compose readiness probes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Docker package-install and Compose-setup readiness loops used raw `docker exec` / `docker inspect` / `docker logs` (and a raw `docker compose down` on cleanup) with **no per-command timeout**. A single stalled Docker daemon RPC could freeze the loop so the nominal 240s / 180s readiness deadline never advanced — the `for _ in $(seq 1 240)` counter loops assumed each probe returned promptly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route every readiness probe, final check, compose up/ps/logs/exec/run/down, and inspect through the existing `docker_e2e_docker_cmd` timeout helper, and convert the fixed-count loops into `SECONDS`-based deadline loops that clamp each probe's `DOCKER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` to the remaining wall-clock budget.

## User Impact

**Before:** One hung `docker exec`/`inspect` during package-install or compose health polling could stall the E2E job well past its intended readiness budget.

**After:** Each Docker probe is bounded by the remaining deadline; a stalled probe is killed, the loop advances, and the script fails closed within the overall readiness window. Compose cleanup `down` is also timeout-bounded.

## Evidence

- Changed: `scripts/e2e/docker-package-install.sh`, `scripts/e2e/compose-setup.sh`, `test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts`
- Production caller path: package-install / compose-setup readiness loops → `DOCKER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT="$probe_timeout" docker_e2e_docker_cmd exec/inspect/...` (`scripts/e2e/docker-package-install.sh:47`).

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

A stalled `docker exec` readiness probe is bounded by the production `docker_e2e_docker_cmd` timeout so the readiness loop fails closed at its deadline instead of blocking forever on the first hung probe.

### Canonical reachability path

`docker-package-install.sh` builds `READY_DEADLINE_AT=$((SECONDS + READY_DEADLINE_SECONDS))` and, each iteration, runs `DOCKER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT="$(docker_e2e_remaining_timeout "$READY_DEADLINE_AT")" docker_e2e_docker_cmd exec "$CONTAINER_NAME" test -f /tmp/openclaw-proof-ready`; `docker_e2e_docker_cmd` (`scripts/lib/docker-e2e-image.sh`) wraps the docker invocation in the host `timeout` with `DOCKER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`.

### Real environment tested

Real shell execution of the production readiness loop with the production helper library sourced (`scripts/lib/docker-e2e-image.sh` → `docker_e2e_docker_cmd`). Two `PATH`-injected fakes stand in for external binaries: a `timeout` that faithfully emulates GNU `timeout` (runs the child under a real wall-clock budget and `SIGKILL`s it on expiry, exit 124) and a `docker` whose `exec` hangs forever (`while true; do sleep 1; done`) while `inspect` reports the container running. No Docker daemon is required; the production helper's timeout wrapping and the deadline loop run for real. macOS, Node v22.23.1 for the Vitest suite.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Direct real-shell run: production readiness loop + docker_e2e_docker_cmd vs a hung `docker exec`.
env PATH="<fake-bin>:/usr/bin:/bin" bash ready-loop.sh "$PWD"   # sources scripts/lib/docker-e2e-image.sh

# Committed real-shell regressions (drive the production helper + source wiring):
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts -- \
  -t 'readiness fails closed|timeout-aware run helper|bounded' --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Direct real-shell run (production readiness loop, hung `docker exec`, 3s deadline):

```text
==> readiness probe (bounded 3s)
[fake-docker] exec: hanging (simulated stuck daemon)
[fake-timeout] probe budget 3s exceeded; killing hung docker child
package install readiness deadline exceeded after 3s
(exit_code=1, wall ≈ 3s)
```

Committed real-shell regressions:

```text
 ✓ docker build helper > package-install readiness fails closed when a single docker exec stalls 4832ms
 ✓ docker build helper > keeps package-backed Docker runs bounded without the shared timeout helper 23ms
 ✓ docker build helper > routes the gateway network client through the timeout-aware run helper 2ms
 ✓ docker build helper > prints in-container Docker client logs through bounded helpers 3ms
 Tests  7 passed | 162 skipped (169)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a hung `docker exec`, the production helper's `timeout` kills the stalled probe at the clamped remaining budget, the loop keeps advancing, and the script fails closed with `package install readiness deadline exceeded after 3s` (exit 1) in ~3s — bounded by the deadline, not blocked forever. Pre-fix, the raw `docker exec` on the first iteration had no timeout and would block the loop indefinitely. The committed source-wiring assertions also pin that neither script contains raw `docker exec ` / `docker inspect ` / `${COMPOSE[@]}` anymore.

### What was not tested

A live Docker E2E lane with a genuinely wedged daemon; the proof exercises the production readiness loop + `docker_e2e_docker_cmd` timeout path against a real hung child on the host.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang (E2E readiness)

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the readiness-loop conversions, the `docker_e2e_docker_cmd` routing, and the real-shell proof output.

target.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway
target.body:
## Summary

- install grouped Claw cron declarations through the gateway-owned `cron.add` API
- persist pending, complete, failed, or removed ownership references keyed by final agent id and declaration id
- expose cron ownership in status, round-trip complete declarations through export, and include exact cron state in remove consent
- disable Claw-owned recurring work before canonical agent deletion, package cleanup, or workspace cleanup
- reuse and extend the canonical agent deletion lifecycle without letting Claws delete unrelated agent files

## Contract

- scheduler mutation stays in the gateway; Claws never write the cron store directly
- declaration keys are scoped as `claw:<agent-id>:<manifest-job-id>`, so package-local ids do not collide globally
- response-lost retries reconcile by declaration key before issuing another `cron.add`
- `main` declarations target `session:agent:<final-agent-id>:main`; `isolated` remains isolated, and strict v1 validation rejects other session modes
- removal calls `cron.remove` before any agent/config mutation and records partial state if recurring work cannot be proven disabled
- canonical `agents.delete` remains responsible for normal agent cleanup; Claws request config/session cleanup while retaining their narrowly managed workspace files for digest-aware removal

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102306 grouped export
- This PR: gateway-owned cron mutation, provenance, status, export, and removal
- Next: #102406 validated MCP ownership

All behavior remains gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- 61 focused cron/lifecycle/schema/provenance/export unit tests
- 15 Claws CLI tests
- 11 canonical agent-delete command tests
- 1 shared agent-cron cleanup test
- 96 gateway agent-mutation tests across gateway projects
- 8 full lifecycle CLI E2E tests
- emitted `cron.add` payload validated by the gateway protocol validator
- Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across 18 code/generated files
- Oxfmt: all 18 files correctly formatted
- `git diff --check`
- Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

The lifecycle tests prove consent-bound add, scheduler-id provenance, response-lost reconciliation, status/export visibility, and removal ordering. A scheduler failure returns partial with `agentRemoved: false`; successful removal calls `cron.remove` before either direct config mutation or the canonical agent-delete delegate.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users exporting a session to HTML could see a broken replacement glyph in compact tool-call previews when a bash command or serialized tool argument was truncated through an emoji.

The corrupted preview was written into the standalone HTML artifact, so it remained visible when the export was saved or shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone viewer truncated compact sidebar strings at raw UTF-16 code-unit boundaries. This is a root-cause, display-layer fix. It does not alter the stored transcript, embedded session data, full tool-call rendering, model input, schema, configuration, or wire format.

## User Impact

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `openclaw-npm-release` workflow could remain stuck in any of its `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks the npm release pipeline and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

All six `git fetch` commands now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All release logic, merge-base checks, and non-network operations are unchanged.

The six locations covered: alpha preflight (L126), tagged release branch-fetch (L268), release-branch resolve fetch (L283), SHA-pinned origin/main fetch (L624), alpha publish preflight (L753), and alpha publish branch-fetch (L914).

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing an npm release runner for the full job timeout before the release begins.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts --run --testNamePattern="bounds openclaw-npm-release git fetch"` ??1 passed.

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each of the production workflow steps, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a Git transport that stalls until `TERM`. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds, the Git fixture observed `TERM`, and none reached the five-second outer watchdog. target.title: fix(ci): bound Docker release BuildKit pre-pull with timeout retries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Docker release "Pre-pull BuildKit image" step used a 4-attempt retry loop around a bare `docker pull` with **no per-attempt process timeout**. When the Docker daemon, DNS, or registry half-opens, the first `docker pull` never returns, so the loop blocks on attempt 1 forever and the remaining retries never run — the job stalls until the runner/job-level timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the BuildKit pre-pull through the existing bounded helper `scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh`, which wraps each `docker pull` in the host `timeout`/`gtimeout` (with a `--kill-after` grace period) and retries. This matches the other CI Docker pull sites and makes a hung pull killable so retries can proceed.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung `docker pull` during a Docker release could stall the job indefinitely (until the runner/job timeout), skipping all retries.

**After:** Each BuildKit pull attempt is bounded (default 180s, `--kill-after=30s`); a hung pull is killed and retried up to four times.

## Evidence

- Changed: `.github/workflows/docker-release.yml`, `test/scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.test.ts`, `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts`
- Production caller path: docker-release `Pre-pull BuildKit image` step → `bash scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh "${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}"` → `openclaw_host_timeout_bin` → `timeout --kill-after=30s "${timeout_seconds}s" docker pull "$image"`.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

A permanently hung first `docker pull` is killed at its per-attempt timeout so a later retry can succeed, instead of blocking the retry loop indefinitely.

### Canonical reachability path

Workflow step → `bash scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh "${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}"` (`.github/workflows/docker-release.yml:137`) → `run_docker_pull` → `"$timeout_bin" --kill-after=30s "${timeout_seconds}s" docker pull "$image"` (`scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh`).

### Real environment tested

Real shell execution of the production `scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh` via `/bin/bash`. Two `PATH`-injected fakes stand in for external binaries: a `timeout` that faithfully emulates GNU `timeout` (runs the child under a real wall-clock budget and `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL`s it on expiry, exit 124) and a `docker` whose first `pull` hangs forever (`while true; do sleep 1; done`) and whose second `pull` succeeds. No Docker daemon is required; the script's own timeout-selection, kill-after, retry, and exit-status logic run for real. macOS, Node v22.23.1 for the Vitest suite.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Direct real-shell run of the production script: hung attempt 1, OK attempt 2.
PATH="<fake-bin>:/usr/bin:/bin" \
  OPENCLAW_DOCKER_PULL_ATTEMPTS=3 OPENCLAW_DOCKER_PULL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2 \
  OPENCLAW_DOCKER_PULL_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=0 \
  bash scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh registry.example/openclaw:test

# Committed real-shell regressions (spawn the script against fake docker/timeout):
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Direct real-shell run (production script, hung first pull bounded and retried):

```text
==> Pull Docker image attempt 1/3: registry.example/openclaw:test
[fake-docker] attempt 1: hanging (simulated stuck registry)
[fake-timeout] budget 2s exceeded (kill-after=30s); killing hung child
Docker pull failed or timed out after 2s: status=124
==> Pull Docker image attempt 2/3: registry.example/openclaw:test
[fake-docker] attempt 2: pull OK
----
script_exit_code=0  approx_wall_s=4  attempts_run=2
```

Committed real-shell regressions (production script via `/bin/bash`):

```text
 ✓ scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh > uses a kill-after grace period when timeout supports it 1022ms
 ✓ scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh > falls back to plain timeout when kill-after is unavailable 460ms
 ✓ scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh > uses gtimeout when timeout is unavailable 491ms
 ✓ scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh > fails fast when timeout and gtimeout are unavailable 6ms
 ✓ scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh > returns the last pull failure status after retries are exhausted 491ms
 ✓ scripts/ci-docker-pull-retry.sh > kills a hung first pull so a later retry can succeed 2384ms
 Tests  6 passed (6)
```

### Observed result after fix

The hung first `docker pull` is killed at the 2s per-attempt budget (`status=124`), the loop advances, attempt 2 succeeds, and the script exits `0` after running exactly 2 attempts. Pre-fix, the bare `docker pull` on attempt 1 would never return, so the loop would block on the first attempt indefinitely and never retry. The `package-acceptance-workflow` test also pins that `docker-release.yml` now calls the bounded helper with `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_PULL_ATTEMPTS: "4"` and no longer contains the raw `if docker pull "${BUILDKIT_IMAGE}"` loop.

### What was not tested

A live GitHub Actions runner pulling `moby/buildkit` against a genuinely wedged registry; the proof exercises the production script's bounding/retry logic against a real hung child on the host.

### Fix classification

bugfix — CI timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the workflow step change and the real-shell proof output.

target.title: fix(tlon): bound outbound channel pokes with request timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tlon outbound `sendText` / `sendMedia` used a duplicated HTTP poke path that called `urbitFetch` without `timeoutMs`. When Urbit's `PUT /~/channel/...` stalled before headers (or an error body stalled after headers), the channel send could hang indefinitely. The sibling SSE path already used `pokeUrbitChannel` with a 30s budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route outbound pokes through the canonical `pokeUrbitChannel` helper (30s wall-clock timeout), reuse cookie/ship normalization from Urbit context, and idle-bound error-body reads so stalled error payloads cannot outlive the poke budget.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung or half-open Urbit channel PUT could leave outbound Tlon sends waiting forever.

**After:** Outbound pokes share the 30s channel-ops timeout (and idle-bounded error body reads), so stalled sends fail closed and release the connection.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.timeout.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.outbound-timeout.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `tlonRuntimeOutbound.sendText` → `createHttpPokeApi.poke` → `pokeUrbitChannel` → `urbitFetch({ timeoutMs })`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Outbound Tlon channel pokes now abort when the PUT never returns headers, and idle-bound a stalled error body, instead of hanging unbounded. Successful pokes still return their id.

### Canonical reachability path

Caller → `createHttpPokeApi.poke` → `pokeUrbitChannel(deps, params)` → `putUrbitChannel` → `urbitFetch({ timeoutMs })` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`; the error path reads via `readResponseTextPrefix(response, limit, { chunkTimeoutMs })` (`extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.ts:61`).

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` Urbit-channel server on `127.0.0.1` with three behaviors — `500` + a partial error body that then stalls forever, a connection that never sends any response, and a normal `204` poke acknowledgement. The exported production `pokeUrbitChannel` is driven directly against those live sockets (public-looking `lookupFn` so the SSRF guard passes, `fetchImpl` connecting to the local server, `timeoutMs: 300` override for a fast budget), Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server: stalled 500 body, never-responding, and 204 success; drive
# the production pokeUrbitChannel against each (budget 300ms):
node --import tsx scripts/proof-tlon-poke-timeout.mts

# Supplemental focused regressions:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.timeout.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.outbound-timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP behavior (production `pokeUrbitChannel` against live sockets):

```text
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 300ms (elapsed 303ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=https://example.com/~/channel/proof-channel
  ok: stalled-error-body poke rejected — Poke failed: 500
  ok: bounded by idle read budget — elapsed=339ms
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 300ms (elapsed 301ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=https://example.com/~/channel/proof-channel
  ok: never-responding poke rejected (not hung) — request timed out
  ok: bounded by request timeout — elapsed=304ms
  ok: unbounded error-body read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: successful poke returns numeric id — 1784293351167

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

Against real sockets: a `500` with a stalled error body makes the poke reject with `Poke failed: 500` in ~339ms (idle-bounded read); a never-responding connection makes the poke reject with `request timed out` in ~304ms (the guarded-fetch deadline). The negative control — a raw `response.text()` on the same stalled error body — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A `204` success still returns the numeric poke id.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real Urbit ship channel endpoint.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the poke path consolidation and caller-path proof output.
